results.title: How to Record an iPhone Screen on Mac | Creavit Studio
results.content:
## The Short Answer

Open Creavit Studio, connect the iPhone to your Mac with a data-capable USB cable, unlock it, tap Trust, and choose iPhone on the recorder screen. Start recording and use the phone normally. The phone's own audio is captured with the video, while the Mac camera and microphone can remain part of the recording when you need narration or a presenter layer.

When you stop, the capture opens directly in Creavit Studio's editor, ready for trimming, 2D or 3D iPhone mockups, Perspective moves, Zoom Motion, backgrounds, camera layouts, overlays, subtitles, and export. There is no separate phone app, AirPlay session, cloud upload, or import step.

The cable matters. A charging-only cable can power the phone without making it available as a capture source.

## What You Need [...] Work through these checks in order:

1. Unlock the iPhone. A locked device may not complete the connection.
2. Accept both prompts. Click Allow on the Mac and Trust on the iPhone, then enter the iPhone passcode.
3. Check Finder. If Finder cannot see the phone, QuickTime and Creavit Studio will not see it either.
4. Try another cable. The cable must support data, not only charging.
5. Try another port or adapter. Hubs and low-quality adapters are common failure points.
6. Disconnect and reconnect. Quit QuickTime or return to the Creavit recorder first, then reconnect the phone.
7. Restart both devices. This clears a capture session that did not close correctly.
8. Update macOS and iOS. Connection fixes often arrive through system updates. [...] ### The recording file is enormous

In QuickTime, use High instead of Maximum unless you specifically need the larger master. In an editor, export the delivery copy with an efficient codec and keep the original project only when you expect to revise it.

### Notifications reveal private information

Use Focus mode before recording, and still watch the final export. Focus reduces interruptions; it does not replace a privacy review.

## A Better Workflow for App Demos

Capturing the phone is only the first half of a good demo. The editing choices determine whether viewers can follow it.

Frame the device, not just the pixels. A phone frame gives the footage scale and makes portrait video feel intentional on a landscape canvas.
